title: SLO sentinel: adaptive multi-signal thresholds for automated rollbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an 'SLO sentinel' service to drive automated rollback decisions during canary / A/B / shadow rollouts. The sentinel will evaluate latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput jointly, apply adaptive threshold tuning, and emit a single rollback decision signal with explainability metadata.
background: Current rollout safeguards rely on static thresholds or single-signal heuristics which either trigger too many false positives (interrupting rollouts) or miss regressions that harm cost/latency. Existing tickets focus on heuristics and orchestrators, but we lack a centrally managed, tunable multi-signal detector that: 1) combines signals into an actionable score, 2) adapts thresholds based on baseline variance and traffic volume, and 3) provides human-readable rationale for rollbacks.
goal: Ship a Sentinel that reduces noisy automated rollbacks by 60% while catching true regressions across latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput. Provide toggles for teams to opt into conservative/aggressive modes, and surface explanations and diagnostics in the Console and rollout webhooks.
proposal:
Implement a separate lightweight service that subscribes to the rollout metrics stream and evaluation harness. For each candidate model and rollout window it will:
  - compute per-signal anomaly scores using a short-window baseline + Bayesian shrinkage to avoid overreacting to low volume
  - normalize signals into a common scale and compute a weighted composite 'rollback score'
  - apply adaptive thresholds that widen during transient spikes and tighten as sample size increases
  - include token-cost drift as a first-class signal (per-token cost delta relative to baseline) so cost regressions can trigger safe rollbacks
  - emit a decision: allow / hold / rollback with an explainability blob (top contributing signals, sample sizes, and confidence)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha for infra and platform owned rollouts (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in for a handful of customer-facing canaries with conservative weighting (4 weeks). Phase 3: GA with UI controls and webhook integration (2 weeks). Each phase will run with 'dry-run' logging before enabling actual orchestrator hooks.
monitoring_signals: latency.p95, latency.p99, request_error_rate, model_generation_errors, throughput.rps, tokens_per_request, per_token_cost_ms, cache_hit_rate, abnormal_control_rate
threshold_tuning_strategy: Use hierarchical priors per-customer and per-model-family to initialize expected metric variance, then update an empirical Bayes posterior during the first N minutes of a rollout. For low-volume rollouts fall back to conservative thresholds. Provide two preset strategies: 'conservative' (higher tolerance to avoid false positives) and 'aggressive' (lower tolerance to catch regressions early). Teams can override with explicit deltas (e.g., latency +30ms) or absolute limits.
auto_rollback_logic: Rollback_score = weighted_sum(normalized_anomaly_scores) where weights are tunable per-metric. Apply a cooldown window of 120s after any decision, require min sample sizes (requests >= 500 or tokens >= 50k) before hard rollback. Hard rollback if: rollback_score > hard_threshold AND confidence > 0.9. Soft hold if: soft_threshold < rollback_score < hard_threshold AND trend_pvalue < 0.05. All auto-decisions must be logged with reason and a link to the artifact that triggered the evaluation.
opt_out_paths: 1) Routes explicitly flagged as 'no-autoretry' in rollout config. 2) Internal infra experiments flagged in the rollout metadata. 3) Canaries with sample size below configured minimum. These are surfaced in the Console and in the webhook payload.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel service subscribes to rollout metrics stream and produces decision events to the rollout orchestrator topic
Dry-run mode logs decisions and explanations for all rollout events without affecting traffic
Conservative and aggressive presets exist and are selectable per-rollout
Rollback events include top-3 contributing signals, sample sizes, and a recommended action
Unit and integration tests cover low-volume behavior, burst spike scenarios, and cost-drift detection
Console UI shows the current sentinel decision, contributing signals, and the historical trend for the canary
testing_plan: Synthetic experiments simulating latency spikes, error bursts, and token-cost regressions across multiple model sizes
Shadow traffic injection to validate detection without user impact
A/B run against current heuristic-based rollback in parallel to measure false-positive/false-negative rates over 30 days
Chaos test: intermittent metrics stream drops to verify graceful degradation and fallback behaviors
implementation_notes: Language: Go service with lightweight in-memory state and Redis backing for model priors
Integrate with metrics pipeline (Prometheus/StatsD -> metrics stream) and existing rollout orchestrator Kafka topic
Expose webhook and Console API endpoints; follow existing auth patterns (service accounts + signed tokens)
Provide a small experimentation harness to tune weights using historical rollout telemetry; store experiments in internal bucket
risks: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks and customer impact if thresholds are misconfigured
Overfitting weights to historical heuristics might miss novel failure modes
Latency added by the Sentinel path must be minimal to avoid slowing the orchestrator decision loop
Privacy: must ensure no raw customer data is stored in the explainability blob; only aggregated metrics and sample counts
